import pandas as pd

# File paths for source tables
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_30/test_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_30/test_1.csv"

# Load Source 0: ['userId', 'movieId', 'tag', 'timestamp']
# index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
df_source0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)

# Load Source 1: ['movieId', 'title', 'genres']
df_source1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Join Source 0 and Source 1 on 'movieId' to get all columns needed for target
# Both have 'movieId' column, which is the key to join on
df_merged = pd.merge(df_source0, df_source1, on='movieId', how='inner')

# Reorder columns to match target schema:
# ['movieId': int, 'title': str, 'genres': str, 'userId': int, 'tag': str, 'timestamp': int]
df_target = df_merged[['movieId', 'title', 'genres', 'userId', 'tag', 'timestamp']]

# Ensure correct dtypes according to target schema
df_target = df_target.astype({
    'movieId': 'int64',
    'title': 'string',
    'genres': 'string',
    'userId': 'int64',
    'tag': 'string',
    'timestamp': 'int64'
})

# Write the result to the specified path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_30/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df_target.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
